title: The first Fats Waller tunes and his dissatisfaction with himself
summary: They cut tunes including 'Chamber Maid's Love Song' and 'Arms Full of Sweetness'; he went home upset at his own playing, and Fats just said goodnight.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: What was the piece, do you remember?
Well, I have a thing there, bomp, bom dah bom, dee, dah dah dah. That's one of the tunes. 'Chamber
"Porter's Love Song, to a instead of Chamber Maid." And "Arms Full of Sweetness." I think that was it.

Dum, duh dah dum, dum ba, dum ba dah. Yeah. "Arm Full of Sweetness," and, and I think the "Chamber Maid" is one. I think that's the first set. And it knocked me out. Hearing myself play. And now I'm my worst enemy.

Well, I didn't like what I heard. Me. I figured it could have been better. Why didn't I do this? Or why didn't I pinch a little more? Or why did I pinch too much? You know. That's the thing, then you start giving yourself the devil. Why? Why? Why? You know. Why don't you rehearse more? Why don't you practice more? Why do you do -- And why? Why?
And I don't know. I went -- when I came home I was very upset.
: Well, it's probably a good way to be.
Maybe. Maybe. But I mean I wasn't happy with what I had done.
Oh, he was -- "bye, see you fellows. Good night." You know.
